LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen much harder than the other defense contractors — down about a third from its high — because its own profit margins slipped, but steady military spending means the underlying business hasn't really changed.

ASML.sentence: ASML is having a quiet stretch and only slightly off its high — the company that makes the one-of-a-kind machines for printing advanced chips is just ticking along, nothing dramatic.

LIN.sentence: Linde is steady this week — the world's biggest supplier of oxygen, nitrogen and other industrial gases keeps signing long contracts and nudging prices up, though right now it's priced no higher than a lesser rival, which is a bit unusual for such a reliable business.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm — it's slipped modestly from its high, and the Azure cloud and AI story just keeps grinding along without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher, which sells the equipment and supplies that labs and biotech companies run on, is looking up because biotech funding is thawing again — and that money tends to flow into their orders a couple of quarters later.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge, the pipeline company that acts like a toll road for North America's oil and gas, is paying a healthy dividend and holding steady — priced fairly rather than a bargain right now.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has pulled back sharply — down more than a quarter from its high — even as big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow-automation and AI-assistant tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore slipped a bit, and its shares are lagging the price of copper it mines and trades — sometimes that gap closes as the shares catch up.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta, the quarry company that sells crushed stone and gravel to road and construction crews, is barely moved — the price it gets per ton of rock is still creeping up nicely, which is the real health check on this business.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA, the big Latin American Coke bottler, is having a good stretch helped by a strong Mexican peso, which makes its earnings look better once converted into US dollars.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras dipped today, but with oil prices well above what it costs the Brazilian oil giant to pump, there's plenty of cash for its famously large dividends — the catch is that these fat profits may be near their peak.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant that moves goods around the world by sea, is quiet this week and trading for less than its fleet of ships would cost to replace.

MA.sentence: Mastercard drifted down a touch and, unusually, is now priced slightly cheaper than Visa even though it typically grows a bit faster — people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so this is mostly market mood, not the business.
